claims.text: A level can take effect before its sleep-time announcement. Some classes and bodies have different notice rules.
claims.proposal: Keep the change, the notice and the recipient as separate events.

claims.text: After certain classes merge, work in one part can advance the whole; maid duties can advance a merged combat path.
claims.proposal: A merged path must state which activities earn shared growth.
claims.delta: E8C branching: activity routing after fusion

claims.text: A total of one hundred across several classes is not a proven ceiling; the page records people above that total.
claims.proposal: Store a per-class threshold separately from a total-level estimate.

claims.text: A person can first perform a method unaided and then have it recognized as a Skill without gaining a level.
claims.proposal: Allow execution-first recognition instead of always reward-first learning.

claims.text: Some joint techniques later work for one contributor; others keep requiring the original team.
claims.proposal: A combined technique needs an explicit participant set and a rule for later solo use.

claims.text: Some prank-related Skills bank the results of antics and spend that credit on stronger effects.
claims.proposal: Let completed jokes supply a stored local currency, rather than merely pricing a silly vow.

claims.text: A ward can receive abilities tied to a designated guardian.
claims.proposal: Record the named provider and the relationship from which each borrowed effect comes.

claims.text: Declared vows can grant Skills outside normal leveling; monastic examples include benefits that deepen with time. The section does not give a general breach penalty.
claims.proposal: Separate growth from keeping a vow from its unverified breach law.
claims.delta: E8D benefit and ramp established; consequence unknown

claims.text: Some conditions are hidden from their bearer, with notice arriving only after removal.
claims.proposal: Allow discovery to lag behind both application and cure.

claims.text: This wiki uses Aspects for body-changing Skills, including a temporary iron-like body.
claims.proposal: Keep source terms namespaced so a body effect is not mistaken for one of our ten descriptive axes.
claims.delta: E8 vocabulary: source term distinct from model axis

claims.text: Quest posting needs knowledge of a real objective and a guaranteed tangible reward; not every imagined target qualifies.
claims.proposal: Separate knowledge eligibility, reward custody and posting authority.
claims.delta: E8B quest giving: admissibility before posting

claims.text: The system can move experience from one activity category to another and alter its multiplier; chess is an example.
claims.proposal: A local system may revise reward routing while retaining a dated rule version.

claims.text: The system distills feats into Skills; the copy need not match the original feat.
claims.proposal: Record the source demonstration and the fidelity of the granted version.

claims.text: A species can finish the trials and still be rejected at the later judgment. Knowledge of the trials is suppressed for many system users.
claims.proposal: Keep task completion, admission and ability to know the gate separate.
claims.delta: E8C gate and grader: collective eligibility

claims.text: Several active artifacts near each other can interfere. Inactive items in a holding bag avoid this; balancing leakage changes the safe load.
claims.proposal: Use active leakage and proximity rather than a fixed count of carried items.

claims.text: Magic-producing monsters can preserve nearby enchantments; leaked magic also benefits the monsters.
claims.proposal: Preservation can create a useful but dangerous local ecology.

claims.text: Horror advancement degrades ordinary classes. This page says lost ranks can restore levels, while Classes and Skills leave restoration unresolved.
claims.proposal: Keep conflicting witness records until a primary scene resolves which losses return.
claims.delta: E8C risk: competing paths with disputed recovery

claims.text: The page distinguishes mana-based casting, emotion-based witchcraft, community-based shamanism and faith-based miracles.
claims.proposal: Make fuel and suppression rules depend on the actual source.
claims.delta: E8B source: different budgets and counters

claims.text: Tags alone do not establish support compatibility. One support can modify several compatible linked skills; several supports can modify one skill.
claims.proposal: Validate an effect contract and its socket group before composition.
claims.delta: E8B composition: reinforces existing typed-contract proposal

claims.text: Duplicate supports do not simply stack. Stronger versions can replace ordinary versions on the same skill.
claims.proposal: Resolve a replacement family before applying modifiers.
claims.delta: E8B composition: precedence and exclusion families

claims.text: Two copies of the same skill in different support groups can provide distinct usable versions.
claims.proposal: Give each configured skill instance its own identity.

claims.text: Leveling a gem strengthens it but can also raise its character-level and attribute requirements.
claims.proposal: Growth can improve an item while making its current host unable to use it.

claims.text: Gem tags belong to the item. A single gem can grant two skills with different behavior and support eligibility.
claims.proposal: Separate labels on the carrier from capabilities of each granted effect.
claims.delta: E8 object: carrier labels versus payload behavior

claims.text: Adding two trigger conditions to the same skill disables it. Different skills can still form a chain with one trigger each.
claims.proposal: Validate each trigger node instead of rejecting or allowing the whole chain by one broad tag.

claims.text: A triggered effect is not counted as a manual use or cast for effects that listen for those events.
claims.proposal: Retain event kind and origin when a reaction creates another event.
claims.delta: E8D breach watchers: semantic event kinds

claims.text: Triggered effects still pay costs. Their cooldowns belong to skills; some systems fire independently while others select one eligible skill at a time.
claims.proposal: Describe automatic delivery, scheduling, cost and cooldown separately.

claims.text: Reservation locks part of a resource while an effect stays active without reducing the resource maximum.
claims.proposal: Track capacity, locked budget and spendable balance separately.

claims.text: A modifier to ordinary spending cost does not necessarily reduce reservation; their calculations differ.
claims.proposal: Bind discounts to a named cost operation.

limits: Selected overview/mechanics sections reviewed; no primary canon certification, no transcluded table completeness.
